input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no usage, licence or fee-compliance audit right against Customer: searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records" and "monitor" return nothing relevant, and §§ 11.5 (Capacity Planning) and 13.2 (AUP) grant IBM no monitoring or verification rights. § 11.3 is an acceptable-use enforcement right — IBM may investigate suspected breaches of the Content/AUP warranty in § 11.2(b) and then remove Content, restrict access or terminate — not verification of our usage or charges, so the AUDIT rule's frequency/notice/cost and underpayment true-up parameters do not apply to it. The absence of any audit right binding us is better than the preferred position and favourable to Bluefly, so no redline is warranted. Noted for the file only (not a deviation): § 11.3 does not require investigators to be bound by confidentiality or expressly limit access to Customer systems, and the notice in p0137 is best-efforts and attaches only to restriction/removal actions; if this clause is opened for other reasons we could ask for notice where practicable, confidentiality obligations on investigators and no access to Customer systems beyond what is necessary. Any suspension/termination remedies in § 11.3(a)-(d) are addressed under the suspension and termination rules rather than here.
